title: The Bosphorus Brief — 27 August 2026
overview: A quieter news day for daily life in Türkiye, dominated by financial and sporting headlines rather than policy shifts. The lira eased slightly as the central bank loosened overnight rates, while regional tensions and a fresh US immigration crackdown continue to ripple outward. A human rights review of the long-running Osman Kavala case and a report on Syrian refugees' safety concerns deserve attention alongside the lighter news.
sections: <parameter name="heading">Money: Lira Steadies as Central Bank Eases
body: The Central Bank cut overnight interest rates by 300 basis points and resumed repo auctions, a technical move aimed at smoothing liquidity. USD/TRY sits at 48.11, EUR/TRY at 56.14, and GBP/TRY at 65.63 — all broadly stable. For residents managing rent, tuition, or salary conversions, this is a normal adjustment rather than a signal of turmoil; Daily Sabah and Zawya both frame it as routine monetary management.
